issue.title: MAVSDK Only Connects to PX4 Autopilot AFTER QGroundControl is Launched!

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed issue! This is, unfortunately, a known issue that I haven't gotten around to fix yet.

The problem is that PX4 starting with v1.13 only starts sending MAVLink once it has received a heartbeat from a GCS or MAVSDK.

Unfortunately, I closed some of the issues mentioning it when I should have left them open. At least I'll now keep this one open until solved.

Also see
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1883
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1908

This workaround should work as long as you use the C++ library (and not mavsdk_server):
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1908#issuecomment-1269316153

Thanks for the speedy reply and for the linked issues! 

Very happy to see that there is a simple work around. For others following this, the proposed changes in #1883 and #1908 worked for me too.

Great to see the #1968 pull request as I am sure it will save others the headache I went through these past days...

Yer, sorry about that. Last time I tried to make the change it seemed too complex, because heartbeats are not sent in a connection but in the `MavsdkImpl`, so I didn't see any easy way without a refactor. Today, I realized there was an easier way.
@OliverHeilmann could you possibly test if the code I threw out here actually works, so either `main` or `v1.4` branch? If so, I'll then do a release.

@julianoes I just built and tested the v1.4 branch while connected to the OrangeCube (running latest PX4 version) and it works! 

For anyone wishing to follow these steps I was testing #1969 and I followed the build instructions linked on the [MAVSDK documentation](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build.html). I am running Linux so my steps were as follows:

Download the source using git:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
```
Make sure to get all the submodules as well:
```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```
Configure first, then build:
```sh
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild/default -H.
cmake --build build/default -j8
```
To install system-wide the command needs to be run with sudo on Linux/macOS:
```sh
sudo cmake --build build/default --target install
```
> :warning: **Conflicting builds**: If you have already installed MAVSDK before!
I had a mavsdk install in the ```/usr/include``` directory, not the ```/usr``` directory as mentioned in the documentation. Similarly, the build library ended up in the ```/usr/local/include``` directory. I deleted the install found in the ```/usr/include``` section to avoid conflicts.
Nice! Thanks you so much @OliverHeilmann. I will cut a release then.
Just tested [1.4.11 release](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v1.4.11) on a Raspberry Pi 4B+ and the updates work as expected.

This issue has been mentioned on **Discussion Forum for PX4, Pixhawk, QGroundControl, MAVSDK, MAVLink**. There might be relevant details there:

https://discuss.px4.io/t/controlling-pixhawk-6c-with-raspberry-pi-4b/30712/7

issue.title: core: always send heartbeat on serial connections

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
PX4 starting with v1.13 does not send heartbeats by default, so we need to initiate the MAVLink connection by sending heartbeats. Therefore, we override the default here and enable sending heartbeats.

Fixes #1967.

timeline.body:

Very happy to see that there is a simple work around. For others following this, the proposed changes in #1883 and #1908 worked for me too.

Great to see the #1968 pull request as I am sure it will save others the headache I went through these past days...

issue.title: Add parameter to enable mavlink stream over USB
issue.body:
From discord thread https://discord.com/channels/1022170275984457759/1032553608417394709

## Describe problem solved by the proposed feature
PX4 no longer sends mavlink via USB unless a heartbeat is received via this channel. This causes trouble to some existing setups, e.g. MAVROS paired with mavlink-router.

## Describe your preferred solution
Have a parameter that lets you choose to always stream mavlink over USB, as was the case up to v1.12.

## Describe possible alternatives
Hardcode it to always send, but that's less clean of a solution


A minimal version of the hardcoded solution can be obtained by moving the four variables https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/8b7c0746800b3597d9418f6442696a1f6fbf3e71/platforms/nuttx/src/px4/common/cdc_acm_check.cpp#L205-L208 out of two if-statements to line https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/blob/8b7c0746800b3597d9418f6442696a1f6fbf3e71/platforms/nuttx/src/px4/common/cdc_acm_check.cpp#L138 and setting `bool launch_mavlink = true;` (replacing `bool launch_mavlink = true;` with `bool launch_mavlink = MAVLINK_USB_EN;` or whatever you want to call the parameter for it to not be hard-coded)

issue.title: Must Open QGroundControl First to Successfully Connect to PX4
issue.body: Hello! I am using `MAVSDK-Java` on an Android device to connect to a Pixhawk `PX4` using an `Orange Cube` and an `ESP8266 Wifi Module`. When using my application with the Gazebo simulator everything works perfectly; however, when connecting to the physical device, I cannot see any information at all besides if I am successfully connected. I am not receiving any telemetry data, battery data, etc. When I open QGroundControl and then go to my app, I am able to see all of the data that I expect. I was wondering if it was related to this issue: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1967 where a fix was created in MAVSDK version `1.4.11`. I know a new maven release was created a month or so ago, but I am curious if a release with MAVSDK `v1.4.11` will resolve my issue. Thank you!

issue.title: Building MAIN breaks Euler Angle Values - ArduCopter (Returns NaN but works in v1.4.16)

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Hello!

I have been following #2031 as I had the same issue with the `GUIDED mode`. I could not get a drone to take off without manually setting it to `GUIDED mode` first. Thankfully, this issue has been solved now, thanks dev team! 

I followed the suggestion of building `main` from source and that has worked nicely so thank you. Unfortunately however, my previously working eulerAngle telemetry gets are now broken/ only return NaN values.

As the title suggests, this issue is raised for ArduCopter (and Rover, Plane etc.) and *not* for PX4 (which I have tried `main` and it works fine).

This is the code I used:
```cpp
mavsdk::Telemetry::EulerAngle eulerAngle = telemetry->attitude_euler();
```
Using `main` I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 07 27](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/6e0744b4-0246-4c74-9e43-6165b9100c0e)

Using `v1.4.16`, I get the following results for euler angle params:
![Screenshot 2023-09-20 at 22 05 02](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/assets/49697817/645fac70-3017-4c64-8ed8-8ff6c3902c0c)

I suspect there is some code change that needs to be modified back to the `v1.4.16` version?

Thanks for your help in advance!
